newsitem.title: NORWAY: Norsk Hydro submits Oseberg South plan.
newsitem.headline: Norsk Hydro submits Oseberg South plan.

text.p: Norsk Hydro ASA, as operator, on Friday submitted a plan for development and operation of the Oseberg South field to the energy ministry, a company statement said.
Oseberg South will be developed as a satellite platform to the Oseberg Field Centre, with extensive use of the infrastructure in the Oseberg area, it said.
Recoverable reserves are estimated to be 53.5 million standard cubic metres of oil and 11 billion standard cubic metres of gas.

Total investments including the oil pipeline to the Field Centre are estimated at 7.6 billion crowns. Pending approval, production will commence in February 2000 from the wells drilled from the Field Centre and in August the same year from the new Oseberg South platform.

The field will be developed with a steel jacket platform for partial processing, drilling and living quarters. The water depth at the platform is 100 metres. Process capacity is 14,900 standard cubic metres per day.

The field has the following ownership breakdown: Norsk Hydro (21.88 percent), Den norske stats oljeselskap AS (Statoil) (56.59 percent), Saga Petroleum ASA (10.14 percent), Dupont's Conoco (7.70 percent) and Mobil (3.70 percent).
